paper.title: Efficient First-Order Contextual Bandits: Prediction, Allocation, and Triangular Discrimination

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with realizability and an online log-loss regression oracle
unmapped: Loss distributions P_{l_t}(.|x_t) and contexts are chosen by a potentially adaptive adversary, but the conditional mean is always f*(x,a) for a fixed f* in F (realizability)
Learner has access to an online log-loss regression oracle with regret bound Reg_KL(T), and the learner knows Reg_KL(T) to tune gamma
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in\brk*{T}$, the learner observes a context $x_t\in\cX$, selects an action $a_t\in\cA$, then observes a loss $\ls_t(a_t)\in\brk*{0,1}$ ... each loss function $\ls_t:\cA\to\brk*{0,1}$ is drawn independently from a fixed distribution $\bbP_{\ls_t}(\cdot\mid{}x_t)$, where $\bbP_{\ls_1},\ldots,\bbP_{\ls_T}$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_T$ are selected by a potentially adaptive adversary. ... There exists a regression function $\fstar\in\cF$ such that for all $t$, $\fstar(x,a) = \En\brk*{\ls_t(a)\mid{}x_t=x}$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Passive (offline) statistical learning / plug-in classification from an i.i.d. dataset with full loss vectors; not an interactive bandit problem.
unmapped: Learner receives n i.i.d. context-loss pairs with the entire loss vector observed and outputs a policy; performance is excess risk L(pi_hat) - L*
settings.definition_quote: We receive a dataset $D_n$ consisting of $n$ context-loss pairs $(x_t, \ls_t)\sim\cD$ \iid, where the entire loss function $\ls_t:\cA\to\brk*{0,1}$ is observed. ... Our goal is to learn a policy $\pihat:\cX\to\cA$ such that the regret (or, excess risk) $L(\pihat) - L^{\star}$ is small

symbols.Reg_KL: regret bound Reg_KL(T) of the online log-loss regression oracle against class F

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Suppose \Cref{ass:realizability,ass:logloss_regret} hold. Then \pref{alg:online_main} guarantees that for all sequences with $\En\brk[\big]{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ls_t(\pistar(x_t))}\leq{} \Lstar$, by choosing $\gamma=\sqrt{\K{} \Lstar/3\RegLog}\vee{}10\K{}$, $\En\brk{\RegCB} \leq 40\sqrt{\Lstar\cdot\K{}\RegLog} + 600\K{}\RegLog.$

results.notes: A = K. Regret defined via realized losses against fixed policy pi*, in expectation equals mean-based regret (proof uses E[Reg]=E[RegBar]), so recorded as pseudo_regret. Efficient given the oracle (O(A) extra per step).

source.quote: If $\cF$ is a finite class, Vovk's aggregating algorithm \citep{vovk1995game} guarantees that $\RegLog \leq \log\abs{\cF}$. With this choice, $\mainalg$ satisfies $\En\brk{\RegCB} \leq \bigoh\prn*{\sqrt{\Lstar\cdot\K{}\log\abs{\cF}} + \K{}\log\abs{\cF}}$.

results.notes: Instantiation of Theorem main; aggregating algorithm over |F| may cost O(|F|) per step.

conditions: F = {(x,a) -> <w, phi(x,a)> : w in simplex Delta_d}
tuning: oracle = continuous exponential weights (Reg_KL = O(d log(T/d))), implemented via log-concave sampling in poly(d,T) time

source.quote: Suppose that $\cF$ takes the form $\cF = \crl*{(x,a)\mapsto{} \tri*{w,\phi(x,a)}\mid{}w\in\Delta_{d}}$ ... With this choice, \mainalg satisfies $\En\brk*{\RegCB} \leq{}\bigoh\prn*{\sqrt{\Lstar\cdot\K{}d\log(T/d)} + \K{}d\log(T/d)}$.

conditions: F = {(x,a) -> (1+<w,phi(x,a)>)/2 : ||w||_2 <= 1} with ||phi(x,a)||_2 <= 1 (also kernel version with RKHS norm <= 1 and K((x,a),(x,a)) <= 1, Example 4)
tuning: oracle = FTRL with log-barrier regularization (Reg_KL = O(sqrt(T log T)))

source.label: ex:highdim
source.quote: Suppose that $\cF$ takes the form $\cF = \crl*{(x,a)\mapsto{} \tfrac{1}{2}(1+\tri*{w,\phi(x,a)})\mid{}\nrm*{w}_{2}\leq{}1}$ ... For this choice, \mainalg satisfies the dimension-independent rate $\En\brk*{\RegCB} \leq{}\bigoh\prn*{(\K\Lstar)^{1/2}T^{1/4} + \K\sqrt{T}}$

results.notes: Dimension-independent. Example 4 (kernels) states the same bound; Example 5 with OGD on logistic loss gives the same expression too. Plugging Reg_KL=O(sqrt(T log T)) would give extra log factors; recorded as printed.

tuning: oracle = improper logistic regression algorithm of Foster et al. 2018 (Reg_KL = O(d log(T/d)))

source.label: ex:logistic
source.quote: we can use the algorithm from \citet{foster2018logistic} to obtain $\RegLog\leq\bigoh(d\log(T/d))$ and $\RegCB\leq\bigoht(\sqrt{\Lstar\cdot{}Ad} + Ad)$.

results.notes: Paper writes Reg_CB without expectation here; presumably expected regret as in Theorem main.

symbols.n_samples: number of i.i.d. training samples n

conditions: algorithm is the least-squares plug-in classifier pi_hat_LS

source.label: thm:least_squares_plugin
source.quote: Let $\cA=\crl{1,2}$ and $\cX=\crl{1,2}$. For every $n>10^8$, there exists a function class $\cF\subseteq(\cX\times\cA\to\brk*{0,1})$ with $\abs{\cF}=2$, and a realizable distribution $\cD$ such that $\Lstar\leq \tfrac{2^{7}}{n}<1$, yet $L(\pihatls) - \Lstar \geq{}2^{-5}\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}}$ with probability at least $1/10$.

results.notes: Out-of-scope statistical learning result. Excess risk lower bound for a specific algorithm (least squares) holding with constant probability 1/10, shows failure of first-order rates.

symbols.n_samples: number of i.i.d. training samples n

conditions: L_star = L(pi*) is the expected loss of the optimal policy (per sample)

source.label: thm:plugin_main
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Suppose that~\pref{assum:plugin_realizability} holds. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $L(\pihatkl) - \Lstar\leq 16\sqrt{\frac{\Lstar \cdot \K{}\rbr{\log|\Fcal| + \log(\K{}/\delta)}}{n}} + 68\frac{\K{}\rbr{\log |\Fcal| + \log(\K{}/\delta)}}{n}.$

results.notes: Out of scope (offline statistical learning). Here L* is an average (per-sample) loss, not cumulative.

symbols.n_samples: number of i.i.d. training samples n
symbols.err_star: misclassification error err(pi*) of the Bayes-optimal classifier

conditions: multiclass classification special case: loss l(a)=1{a != y}

source.label: thm:multinomial_plugin
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and consider the multiclass classification setting under~\pref{assum:plugin_realizability}. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\err(\pihatkl) - \err(\pi^\star) \leq 8\sqrt{\frac{\err(\pi^\star) \cdot 2\log(|\Fcal|/\delta)}{n}} + 34\frac{\log(|\Fcal|/\delta)}{n}.$

results.notes: Only a proof sketch is given. Out-of-scope setting; removes the A factor.
